# sigma_deployment_policy (Resource)

A Sigma deployment policy: controls how content is promoted into tenant organizations, including which source-swap policies apply and whether input table data is copied. Use sigma_deployment_policy_file and sigma_deployment_policy_tenant to attach files and target tenants.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# version_tag_id is a content-scoped concept (a workbook's version history)
# that this provider does not manage — supply the real ID from Sigma's UI or
# API. It is set once at creation; changing it forces replacement.
resource "sigma_deployment_policy" "prod_rollout" {
  name                  = "Prod Rollout"
  name_in_tenant        = "Production"
  version_tag_id        = "<version-tag-id>"
  source_swap_policies  = [sigma_source_swap_policy.dev_to_prod.id]
  copy_input_table_data = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name of the deployment policy.

### Optional

- `copy_input_table_data` (Boolean) Whether input table data is copied to receiving tenant organizations when deploying documents. Only applies to input tables editable in draft mode.
- `name_in_tenant` (String) Name to use for the workspace created by the deployment policy in the receiving tenant. Defaults to `name` when omitted.
- `source_swap_policies` (List of String) IDs of sigma_source_swap_policy resources used to swap connections when deploying documents.
- `use_dependencies_workspace` (Boolean) Whether implicit dependencies are placed in a different workspace, separate from the deployment workspace.
- `version_tag_id` (String) Version tag ID pinned at creation. Not patchable — Sigma's update endpoint does not accept this field, so changing it forces replacement.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import sigma_deployment_policy.example '<deployment_policy_id>'
```
